skill.name: email-notify
skill.description: Send task completion emails through a configured SMTP server with device, project, status, and summary details.
skill.summary: Send configurable SMTP notifications when Claude or Codex tasks finish.
skill.author: caopulan

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, local validation, and scoped configuration reads. Confirmed risks include shell-profile credential storage, optional unencrypted SMTP authentication, environment access to the SMTP password, and intended outbound SMTP connections.

remediation.issue: The setup stores the SMTP password in .bashrc or .zshrc.
remediation.suggestion: Use a credential manager or an invocation-scoped secret source. Do not export the password from a general shell startup file.

remediation.issue: Authenticated SMTP is allowed when both SSL and STARTTLS are disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Reject authenticated connections unless SSL or STARTTLS is enabled. Permit plaintext SMTP only for unauthenticated, explicitly approved local relays.

remediation.issue: Notifications can include sensitive task summaries and project metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Require a dry-run before first use, document the transmitted fields, and keep secrets out of task titles and summaries.

content.value_statement: Finished agent tasks can be missed when users leave the terminal. This skill sends concise SMTP emails with task status and project context.
actual_capabilities: Sends plain-text completion emails with device, project, status, and summary fields.
Supports authenticated SMTP over SSL or STARTTLS.
Accepts multiple recipients separated by commas or semicolons.
Resolves project names from arguments, AGENTS.md, or the current directory.
Previews connection details and email content with a dry-run option.
limitations: Requires Python 3, a reachable SMTP server, and user-provided environment configuration.
Sends plain-text messages only and does not support HTML or attachments.
Runs only when an agent invokes the helper script; it does not monitor tasks independently.
Does not redact secrets from user-provided titles or summaries.

use_cases.title: Monitor Long Development Tasks
use_cases.description: Receive an email when a long Codex implementation or test run finishes.

use_cases.title: Track Remote Agent Runs
use_cases.description: See completion status and project context without maintaining a terminal connection.

use_cases.title: Report Automation Outcomes
use_cases.description: Send concise success, failure, or blocked summaries after scheduled agent work.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Basic Completion Email
prompt_templates.prompt: Send a completion email for this finished task. Use title [title], status [status], and summary [summary]. Preview it before sending.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants one clear notification.

prompt_templates.title: Use the Detected Project Name
prompt_templates.prompt: Notify me that [task] finished with status [status]. Resolve the project name automatically and summarize the result without secrets.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants project context without specifying a name.

prompt_templates.title: Report a Failed Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Send an email for the failed task [task]. State the failure status, summarize the cause, and list the next safe action.
prompt_templates.scenario: An operator needs an actionable failure notification.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Send a Team Notification
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a completion notification for [task] and [project]. Dry-run it, verify recipients and transport security, then send after approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs controlled delivery to multiple recipients.

best_practices: Run a dry preview before sending to new recipients or through a new SMTP server.
Keep task titles and summaries concise, accurate, and free of secrets.
Use SSL or STARTTLS whenever SMTP authentication is enabled.
anti_patterns: Do not place SMTP passwords in shared files, prompts, task summaries, or source control.
Do not send notifications to unverified recipient lists.
Do not disable transport encryption for authenticated internet SMTP servers.

faq.question: Which SMTP modes are supported?
faq.answer: The helper supports implicit SSL, STARTTLS, and plain SMTP. Authenticated connections should always use SSL or STARTTLS.

faq.question: Can one notification reach multiple recipients?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure recipient addresses as a comma-separated or semicolon-separated list.

faq.question: How is the project name selected?
faq.answer: An explicit argument has priority. Otherwise, the helper checks AGENTS.md and then uses the project directory name.

faq.question: Can I preview a message without sending it?
faq.answer: Yes. The dry-run option prints connection details and message content without opening an SMTP connection.

faq.question: Does the skill remove secrets from summaries?
faq.answer: No. Users and agents must exclude credentials, tokens, personal data, and other sensitive content.

faq.question: Does the skill send notifications automatically?
faq.answer: No. An agent must invoke the helper after a task or follow a project instruction that requests notification.
